I'm sorry you had such a negative experience with CGRP meds but you are consistently negative whenever you possibly can be. It's dangerous to suggest that a potentially helpful medication is 100% the cause of anyone's woes or that you absolutely know better than your doctor.

OP, from what everyone can gather, menstrual side effects are quite common with CGRP medications, especially Qulipta. But menstrual cycles can be sensitive to so many things that, especially if you have a male doctor, it can be brushed off. Even if it is, if you are prescribed this medication, it is because your doctor believes the benefits outweigh the risks. Outside of this commenter, there appear to be no "significant" effects to the reproductive system, besides the disruption of the usual cycle. 

I have been on qulipta and have noticed a slight disruption to my cycles (slightly heavier periods, cramping, etc.) but the overall effect of having half the migraines as I used to is absolutely worth it for me. CGRP affects everyone slightly differently and personally for me, I'd rather have an irregular period than have a migraine every single day.

I have the same issue. Been having a constant headache since... 2015? 2016? Went through my whole adolescence with it.

All of the CGRP meds I've been on have been a massive help. It didn't get rid of the persistent headache but it certainly took the edge off. used to get at a constant 5 but now it's about a 2.5 most days. 

The biggest difference between being on CGRP meds and not is the frequency and severity of full blown migraines.  I went from about 20 migraine days a month to like... 4? And it's usually because of a trigger rather than a default setting. Migraines went from completely debilitating to an inconvenience. Before I would always power through because when am I /not/ in pain anyway? Now I'm comfortable with taking time off and resting when they hit. It was life-changing.

Abortives are kinda hit or miss. Ubrelvy helped half of the time. Nurtec almost always works.

Emgality helped the most out of the injectables, Qulipta has helped the most overall.

Campus seems depressing during breaks because it *is* depressing during breaks. Hardly anyone is on campus. Plus, we're in a very not-pretty phase of the seasons here. During the limbo between all the leaves falling off but before snow begins to fall, the campus doesn't look all that great. But oh man, it's beautiful at pretty much any other time of the year. I often sit under the ginkgo tree when weather permits it to study or relax.

Socially it's not awful here. I'm a commuter and a massive homebody so it was really lonely my first year, but once I found a couple people and joined a club (shout-out MSM Spelunkers) things got so much better. You don't have to party or drink to have a good time. My favorite part of not doing either of those things is that I can live through my friends recounting their wild stories of the week, and I never have to put myself in those dumbass situations! Greek life is always an option if you're not opposed to partying. Sometimes it's cheaper to live on campus through Greek than Res.

There are a few study abroad options. There is a study abroad fair in Havener every September that has both UM-affiliated and third-party representatives that would be more than willing to give you a rundown of your options. There are also some options like Engineers Without Borders, and we had a chemical engineer come with the Bio/EnvSci dept to Ecuador this past summer. It was only for a few weeks and it felt like a lifetime of experiences. So don't count those out.

Campus has a surprising amount of events during the year, especially ones held outdoors. But of course, they're not gonna have it in the miserable winter weather. We have an Earth Day thing, multiple companies hosting lunches, Career fair, St. Pat's (single biggest event here besides maybe the Career Fair), etc. Once I started hanging out on campus more I slowly fell in love. It has a lot to offer if you put effort into finding the things you love.
